about.title: Rocklin Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Rocklin residents run into defective products in everyday settings — a faulty ladder at a Sierra College Boulevard job site, a malfunctioning appliance at home, a car part that fails near Sunset Boulevard or I-80. Under California's strict liability rules, you generally don't have to prove the manufacturer was careless; you only need to show the product was defective in design, manufacturing, or warning, and that the defect caused your injury. That standard applies whether the product came from a big-box retailer or a small distributor, and liability can extend to any link in the supply chain. Because these cases often hinge on physical evidence, holding onto the item, its packaging, and any instructions matters. We evaluate the product, the injury, and next steps directly, all on a contingency basis so there's no fee unless there's a recovery.
commonInjuries: Burns from malfunctioning appliances or batteries
Lacerations from faulty tools or machinery

Poisoning or chemical exposure from mislabeled products
Traumatic injuries from failed safety equipment

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Path
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, you may not need to prove the manufacturer was negligent — just that the defect existed and caused harm.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which widens the pool of parties we can pursue on your behalf.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters — We Help You Get Guidance Fast
items.desc: Our team can advise you early on how to document and preserve the defective item itself, which is often central evidence in these claims.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California's strict liability framework generally allows you to focus on showing the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, rather than proving negligence. Our team can walk you through how this applies to your specific situation.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Try to keep the item, its packaging, and any manuals or receipts exactly as they are, without altering or repairing it. This physical evidence is often critical to a product liability claim, and we can advise on safe storage.

items.question: I was hurt by a product near Sierra College Boulevard in Rocklin — does location matter for my claim?
items.answer: The location itself isn't usually the legal issue in a product liability case, but it can help establish where and how the injury occurred. What matters more is the product's defect and the harm it caused, which our team can evaluate regardless of where in Rocklin it happened.

items.question: Is there a cost to contact us?
items.answer: No. There's no cost to reach out, and our team typically works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless we recover money for you. There's no obligation to move forward after speaking with us.
